# Node Exporter Receiver

Receives host metrics by embedding the Prometheus
[node_exporter](https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter)
directly in the OpenTelemetry Collector.

## Configuration

This draft embeds the unreleased runtime from
[prometheus/node_exporter#3661](https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/pull/3661),
pinned to commit `05c0591a67bce359eaf472b6126db40fd607b79c` through a temporary
module replacement. Replace that pin with an upstream release before merging.
The distribution manifest repeats the replacement because Go does not propagate
replacements from dependency modules.

```yaml
receivers:
  node_exporter:
    scrape_interval: 15s
    exporter_config:
      collector_disable_defaults: true
      collectors:
        cpu: true
        meminfo: true
        filesystem: true
      cpu:
        enable_guest: true
      path:
        proc_fs: /proc
        sys_fs: /sys
        root_fs: /
        udev_data: /run/udev/data

exporters:
  debug:
    verbosity: detailed

service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [node_exporter]
      exporters: [debug]
```

`exporter_config` maps to upstream `config.Config`; keys use snake_case.
All upstream collection options are available, including `textfile.directories`,
`filesystem.mount_timeout`, and per-collector filters. Duration fields accept
strings such as `5s`. The receiver uses upstream defaults for omitted settings.
With `collector_disable_defaults: false` (the default), the `collectors` map
overrides individual collector defaults. With it set to `true`, only explicitly
enabled collectors run. Collector availability depends on the operating system
and upstream build tags; unknown names cause startup to fail.

Filesystem and diskstats include filters require clearing their corresponding
default exclude filter, for example:

```yaml
exporter_config:
  filesystem:
    mount_points_exclude: ""
    mount_points_include: '^/data($|/)'
```

Multiple named receivers may use different paths, textfile directories,
collector selections, and scrape intervals. For containerized deployments,
mount the host filesystems and configure the matching `path` values. Collectors
using syscalls, local sockets, or netlink still observe the Collector process's
namespaces, as they do in the standalone Node Exporter.

The receiver gathers directly from a Prometheus registry. It does not start a
Node Exporter HTTP server, parse CLI flags, or include the standalone binary's
Go/process/build metrics. Collection metrics retain their upstream names and
labels, including `node_scrape_collector_success`.

## Draft limitations

Receiver shutdown calls the shutdown function of its own upstream Runtime.
The pinned runtime closes ethtool sockets, stops and closes perf profilers, and
closes supervisord's idle HTTP connections. Repeated shutdown is supported.
Collector updates no longer accept a context, so shutdown does not cancel
in-flight collection. Stop gathering before releasing a runtime's resources.

The upstream runtime keeps collector configuration, the supervisord client, NTP
leap state, and filesystem stuck-mount tracking separate for each instance.
The pinned runtime now frees the FreeBSD devstat device buffer and rolls back
tracepoint profilers when initialization fails. This remains a draft integration
until the runtime is released. The supervisord Unix-socket transport still
inherits HTTP proxy settings, which can break collection when `HTTP_PROXY` is
configured. Perf CPU selections should not contain duplicate CPUs or overlapping
ranges: the pinned collector overwrites handles for repeated CPUs and cannot
close all of them on shutdown.

## Validation

`go test -race ./...` checks configuration defaults and rejection, two concurrent
textfile receivers with distinct fixture values, startup-context cancellation,
independent runtime resource cleanup, and cleanup on registration failure. Linux
additionally verifies CPU and meminfo runtimes with separate checked-in procfs
fixtures and no flag initialization.
